rounds.response:
1) HCP — Hepatic (Option A — minimal edit): "Elevations of serum transaminases (ALT and/or AST) were observed in clinical trials and were generally asymptomatic and reversible on interruption or discontinuation of therapy; obtain baseline LFTs (ALT, AST, bilirubin), repeat at 2–4 weeks after initiation and periodically thereafter; interrupt treatment if ALT or AST ≥3×ULN with symptoms of liver injury or ≥5×ULN without symptoms; discontinue treatment if ALT or AST ≥8×ULN, or if jaundice or other signs of clinically significant liver injury develop."  
2) HCP — Hepatic (Option B — alternative streamlined): "Transient, generally reversible increases in ALT/AST were reported; obtain baseline LFTs and repeat at 2–4 weeks and periodically; interrupt therapy for ALT/AST ≥3×ULN with symptoms or ≥5×ULN without symptoms and discontinue for ALT/AST ≥8×ULN or if jaundice or other clinically significant liver injury occurs."  
3) HCP — Hypersensitivity (Option A — minimal edit): "Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported; if a serious allergic reaction occurs, stop the product immediately, provide appropriate emergency medical treatment, and do not rechallenge the patient."  
4) Patient leaflet (Option A — minimal edits): "Liver: Your doctor will do blood tests before you start and again 2–4 weeks after starting, and sometimes during treatment; call your doctor right away if you get yellow skin/eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or ongoing nausea/vomiting. Allergy: Serious allergic reactions can happen — stop taking the medicine and get medical help right away if you have swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing, or hives; do not take the medicine again."  
5) Limitations of Use / Use in Specific Populations (minimal edit): "Efficacy has not been established in patients with severe renal impairment; use is not recommended in this population (see Use in Specific Populations). No dosing recommendations are available for patients with severe renal impairment (see Dosage and Administration)."

The guidance suggests repeating these tests after two to four weeks and interrupting treatment if there are significant elevations. However, referencing the same section within itself feels a bit off. I think it’s best not to use "see Warnings..." within the Warnings section.

Moving to the section on specific populations, I notice the comment on severe renal impairment. Instead of referencing a specific number, it feels safer to standardize it as "(see Dosage and Administration)." This way, I avoid inventing numbers while still providing essential information.
